gap: No result ChatGPT got gives a measured usable capacity for any kit near 1,500 Wh. Michael Barton at techtest.org measured the ALLPOWERS S2000 (rated 1,500 Wh) delivering only 1,123 Wh on AC at 200 W and 1,133 Wh at 1,200 W, which is 75–76% of its label. StorageReview measured the S2000 Pro (sold as 1,500 Wh at the time of the test, now listed at 1,451 Wh) delivering 920 Wh at 350 W, and the unit shut off with 22% still showing.
standout_why: Pages compared: powersized.com/solar-generator-kits (cited, 'We have not tested these units in person'; its 1,536 Wh Jackery rows carry only modelled refill hours and Jackery's own estimates), stormwatts.com same-panel-watts (cited, no measured figures for any 1,200–1,800 Wh unit; ALLPOWERS absent; its only owner reading is on a 2,042 Wh Explorer 2000 Plus), and powersized.com/best/solar-generator (top result, only OutdoorGearLab's 950 Wh for the 1,152 Wh BLUETTI AC180, which is outside this size band). None gives a measured usable Wh, charge efficiency or idle draw for the Jackery 1500 v2, the Jackery 1500 Ultra or the ALLPOWERS S2000 / S2000 Pro.
decides: This doesn't change the pick, but it reframes our ALLPOWERS rows. On AC the S2000 behaves like a 1,100 Wh station, and the S2000 Pro tested at about 920 Wh, so a shopper who needs 1,500 Wh of usable AC energy should not count on the label. Price per Wh still favours ALLPOWERS. At the measured AC figure, the S2000 + SF200 link price of $612.90 works out to $0.54 per delivered Wh ($612.90 / 1,133 Wh). The Jackery 1500 v2 kit ChatGPT showed at $1,279 works out to $0.83 per rated Wh ($1,279 / 1,536 Wh); no measured figure exists to compare against. Both ALLPOWERS tests date from 2023, and both reviewers note the S2000 line's ternary-lithium (NMC) cells. The page should say which kit wins on cost per measured Wh and which only on label Wh, and should not claim that a measured Jackery figure exists.
